summary: The bill prevents and addresses employment discrimination, including harassment, by requiring employers to adopt nondiscrimination policies and training, expanding coverage to independent contractors/interns and clarifying that sexual orientation/gender identity discrimination is unlawful sex discrimination, strengthening remedies and statutes of limitations, prohibiting mandatory arbitration of work disputes, and authorizing grants for prevention, advocacy, and legal assistance.

scores.thoughts: The bill authorizes new appropriations for the EEOC (including a new Office of Education and Outreach and revolving fund uses), multiple studies and surveys by federal agencies, and several grant programs for prevention, legal assistance, and state advocacy systems. These provisions directly expand federal spending on new enforcement, research, and assistance activities.
The bill contains no provisions altering tax rates, deductions, credits, or revenue collection mechanisms.
The bill contains no provisions addressing health insurance coverage, public programs, or market-based healthcare delivery.
The bill contains no provisions related to firearms, regulations, or Second Amendment rights.
The bill contains no provisions altering immigration pathways, enforcement, or border policy.
While the bill expands protections against pregnancy-related discrimination, it does not address abortion access or restrictions.
The bill contains no provisions affecting military or defense budgets or policy.
The bill contains no provisions related to environmental regulations or protections.

The bill includes grants for legal assistance to low-income workers facing discrimination and phases in higher minimum wages for tipped employees. These have tangential effects on low-wage worker support but are primarily labor and civil rights measures rather than direct welfare expansions.
The bill contains no provisions addressing schools, school choice, or federal education policy.
The bill contains no provisions related to drug enforcement or decriminalization.
The bill focuses exclusively on civil employment remedies and does not address criminal sentencing, policing, or rehabilitation.
The bill contains no provisions related to tariffs, trade agreements, or globalization.
New authorized spending for EEOC activities, grants, and studies could increase deficits, but the bill does not directly address debt reduction or fiscal policy.

The bill explicitly amends Title VII and related statutes to clarify that sexual orientation and gender identity discrimination constitute unlawful sex discrimination, extends protections to additional workers, and limits RFRA defenses. This is a core purpose of the legislation.
The bill contains no provisions related to foreign assistance.
The bill contains no provisions related to voting access or election integrity.
The bill contains no provisions regulating technology companies or data privacy.

The bill substantially strengthens worker protections by expanding coverage to more employers and workers (including independent contractors and interns), prohibiting mandatory arbitration of work disputes, extending statutes of limitations, broadening damages, and creating new enforcement mechanisms and grants. These are core labor and worker-rights expansions.

The bill explicitly provides that the Religious Freedom Restoration Act shall not provide a claim or defense under Title VII and related laws, while expanding anti-discrimination protections. This prioritizes civil rights enforcement over religious exemptions.
